title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 126
paragraphs: To this end came the great prosperity of Polycrates, as Amasis king of Egypt had foretold. But not long afterwards retribution overtook Oroetes in turn for the murder of Polycrates. For after the death of Cambyses and the reign of the Magians, Oroetes remained at Sardis and rendered no service to the Persians, who had been deprived of their empire by the Medes. Moreover, during this time of disturbance he killed Mitrobates, the governor in Daskyleion who had reproached him about Polycrates, and he killed Cranaspes son of Mitrobates as well, both men of repute among the Persians. Besides various other outrages, once when a messenger had come to him from Darius, displeased with the message he brought, he killed him on his way back, having set men in ambush along the road; and after killing him, he made away with the bodies both of the man and of his horse.
